Recursive feature elimination with held-out evaluation

Source: R/fs_recursivefeature.R
fs_recursivefeature.Rd

Finds how few predictors a model needs before its resampled performance starts to drop. fs_recursivefeature() splits the data into stratified training and test rows, runs caret::rfe() on the training rows, and scores the chosen subset on the test rows. It can also one-hot encode the predictors first and fit a final caret model on the selected ones.

Usage

fs_recursivefeature(
  data,
  target,
  sizes = NULL,
  train_ratio = 0.8,
  rfe_control = list(method = "cv", number = 5),
  train_control = list(method = "cv", number = 5),
  model_method = "rf",
  handle_categorical = FALSE,
  return_final_model = FALSE,
  seed = NULL,
  verbose = FALSE,
  parallel = FALSE
)

Arguments

data

A data.frame or data.table holding the target and the candidate predictors (every other column). It needs at least one row, unique non-empty column names, and at least two candidate predictors after any one-hot encoding. It is converted to a plain data.frame on entry.

target

Single string naming the target column; a column index is not accepted. A factor, character, or logical target means classification (unused factor levels are dropped), anything else regression. The target may not contain missing or infinite values.

sizes

Whole-number subset sizes to evaluate; fractional sizes are an error. Default NULL uses 1:p, where p is the predictor count after any one-hot encoding. Values outside [1, p] are dropped with a warning, and the call stops if none are left.

train_ratio

Training proportion of the stratified split, strictly between 0 and 1. Default 0.8.

rfe_control

List of arguments for caret::rfeControl(). Default list(method = "cv", number = 5).

  • method and number are required. method is one of "cv", "repeatedcv", "LOOCV", "boot", "boot632", "LGOCV" or "test" (matched ignoring case), and number must be at least 2 for "cv" and "repeatedcv". With "repeatedcv" and no repeats, caret's default of 1 is used and a warning says so.

  • functions is the caret RFE function set, default caret::rfFuncs. A supplied set must contain the functions summary, fit, pred, rank, selectSize and selectVar.

  • index, indexOut and indexFinal are an error: resampling runs on the internal training split, so row numbers built for data would point at the wrong rows.

  • allowParallel is dropped with a warning; use parallel instead. verbose, if present, overrides the verbose argument for caret::rfe().

train_control

List of arguments for caret::trainControl(), used only when return_final_model = TRUE and then checked, together with model_method, before the search starts. It must contain method, and also number unless method = "none" (at least 2 for "cv" and "repeatedcv"). index, indexOut and indexFinal are an error, for the same reason as in rfe_control. Unless set here, allowParallel follows parallel, so a sequential call does not use a foreach backend you registered yourself. Default list(method = "cv", number = 5).

model_method

Single string: the caret model key for the final model, such as "rf" or "lm". It must be in caret's built-in model library. Used only when return_final_model = TRUE. Default "rf".

handle_categorical

Logical; one-hot encode the predictors with full-rank dummies, fitted on the training rows and applied to the test rows. A dummy name (<variable><level>) that matches another column is an error. Function sets that work on a model matrix, such as caret::lmFuncs, rank dummy columns rather than factors, so they need handle_categorical = TRUE when factor predictors are present; without it the call stops with an error that says so. Default FALSE.

return_final_model

Logical; train a final caret model on the training rows using the selected predictors and return it as model (the rfe object stays in details$rfe). Near-zero-variance and linearly dependent predictors are dropped from the selected set first, each with a warning, and the survivors are recorded in details$final_model_variables. Default FALSE.

seed

Optional whole number within the range of an R integer. Fractional or out-of-range values are an error, not truncated. Default NULL, which never seeds. See "Seeds and parallel runs" in Details.

verbose

Logical; print progress messages and let caret::rfe() report its own progress, unless rfe_control$verbose overrides the latter. Default FALSE.

parallel

Logical. TRUE registers a two-worker PSOCK cluster (capped at the detected core count) for the duration of the call, then stops it and restores whichever foreach backend was registered before. Requires the suggested packages 'foreach' and 'doParallel'. The RFE resampling and the final model's resampling both follow this setting. A custom function set such as caret::caretFuncs builds its own inner caret::train() control and is not covered. Default FALSE.

Value

An object of class fs_result with:

selected

Character vector of the predictors RFE kept: caret's optVariables at the optimal subset size.

scores

Named numeric vector with one entry per candidate predictor: its importance in the full-size fit (all candidates present), averaged over every resample. caret::varImp() on the rfe object instead averages a predictor only over the resamples where it survived to the optimal size, which inflates marginal predictors and omits predictors that never survived. When the function set records no per-resample importance, the caret::varImp() values are used instead. NULL when neither is available.

method

"rfe".

task

"classification" or "regression", inferred from the target.

model

The final caret::train model when return_final_model = TRUE, otherwise the rfe object.

details

A list with:

  • rfe: the caret rfe object, present even when model holds the final model.

  • optimal_size: the subset size RFE chose.

  • test_metrics: caret::postResample() on the test rows, the only held-out estimate on the result.

  • resampling_results: the RFE resampling summary over candidate sizes, computed inside the training rows.

  • variable_importance: the caret::varImp() data.frame. It averages each predictor only over the resamples where it survived to the optimal size, and selected follows caret's optVariables rule, which is weighted the same way.

  • preprocessor: the dummyVars encoder, or NULL when handle_categorical = FALSE.

  • train_index, test_index: row indices into data for the two partitions.

  • final_model_variables: the predictors the final model used after near-zero-variance and linear-combination filtering, or NULL when no final model was requested.

  • n_features: the number of candidate predictors offered to RFE, counted after one-hot encoding and after constant predictors were removed.

call

The matched call.

Details

Recursive feature elimination (RFE) fits a model on all candidate predictors and ranks them by importance, then refits on the top k for each subset size k in sizes, inside every resample of rfe_control. The size with the best resampled performance wins, so you do not have to pick a cutoff yourself. The price is one model fit per candidate size per resample, which makes RFE one of the slowest methods in featR. The answer is also tied to the model family in rfe_control$functions (random forests by default): it tells you which predictors that model needs, not which predictors are informative in general.

The honest performance estimate is details$test_metrics. The Validation and leakage article lists which numbers in each featR result are held out and which are optimistic.

Required packages

'caret' is always required. The default function set, caret::rfFuncs, fits random forests and needs 'randomForest'; so does the default final model (model_method = "rf") when return_final_model = TRUE. To avoid random forests, pass another set, for example rfe_control = list(method = "cv", number = 5, functions = caret::lmFuncs). Classification also needs 'e1071', because the metrics come from caret::postResample(). parallel = TRUE needs 'foreach' and 'doParallel'. All of these are checked before any model is fitted.

What the held-out rows see

Everything learned from data is learned on the training rows: the one-hot encoder, the factor levels the test columns are aligned to, the elimination itself, and the final model. The test rows play no part in choosing either the predictors or the subset size.

details$test_metrics applies caret::postResample() to the test-row predictions of the fitted rfe object, which is caret's refit on all training rows restricted to the optimal subset. It is the only held-out estimate on the result. Two other summaries reuse the training rows and are optimistic:

  • details$resampling_results is the resampled performance at each candidate size, computed inside the training rows. The size RFE picked is the best of these, so its entry is biased upward.

  • With return_final_model = TRUE, model$results reports train_control resampling inside the same training rows, on predictors that were already chosen using those rows.

Reading the metrics

The metrics are caret's. For regression they are RMSE, Rsquared and MAE, where Rsquared is the squared Pearson correlation between predictions and observations, not 1 - SSE/SST. It is never negative and ignores bias and scale errors, so it cannot be compared with an R2 defined as 1 - SSE/SST, such as details$metrics$R2 from fs_randomforest(). For classification they are Accuracy (the proportion of test rows classified correctly) and Kappa (Cohen's kappa, accuracy corrected for chance agreement).

Data preparation and requirements

  • Infinite values (Inf, -Inf) anywhere in data are an error.

  • Missing values in the training predictors are an error; impute or drop incomplete rows before calling. Missing values in the test rows are not imputed. Depending on the function set, predict() then either stops (random forests) or returns NA for those rows, which caret::postResample() leaves out of details$test_metrics. A warning reports how many rows were left out.

  • Character and logical predictors become factors. Factor predictors keep only the levels observed in the training rows; a test value with a level the training rows never saw becomes missing, with a warning.

  • Predictors that are constant on the training rows (a single value, or a factor with one observed level) are removed with a warning before RFE. They carry no information, and a random forest fitted on a single constant predictor never returns.

  • Predictor names that are not syntactic R names, such as "a b", break caret's function sets, so the rfe object and the final model use their make.names() versions. selected, scores, details$variable_importance and details$final_model_variables report the original names.

  • With handle_categorical = TRUE, the encoded test rows are checked against the input row count, so an encoding that loses rows is an error instead of a misaligned metric.

Seeds and parallel runs

seed covers the split and the RFE resampling. It is applied for the duration of the call only, and the previous RNG state is restored on exit. With seed = NULL the call draws from your current RNG stream without reseeding it. Under parallel = TRUE, a seed also sets rfe_control$seeds = NULL unless you supplied seeds, so caret draws one seed per resample from the locally seeded RNG. That is what makes two seeded parallel runs agree. The workers also get L'Ecuyer-CMRG streams, but those alone would not be enough, because foreach hands each resample to whichever worker is free. A seeded parallel run need not match a seeded sequential one, because the sequential run keeps caret's default seeds = NA. See Reproducibility and parallelism.

See also

The Wrapper methods guide, which runs this function on a worked example.

Examples

if (requireNamespace("caret", quietly = TRUE) &&
    requireNamespace("randomForest", quietly = TRUE) &&
    requireNamespace("e1071", quietly = TRUE)) {
  res <- fs_recursivefeature(
    iris,
    target = "Species",
    sizes = 1:4,
    rfe_control = list(method = "cv", number = 3),
    seed = 42
  )
  print(res$selected)
  print(res$details$optimal_size)
  # the only held-out estimate on the object
  print(res$details$test_metrics)
}
#> [1] "Petal.Length" "Petal.Width"  "Sepal.Length"
#> [1] 3
#>  Accuracy     Kappa 
#> 0.9333333 0.9000000
